name: grpc-go-suspendable-resolver-sessions
instr:
gRPC-Go cannot pause and resume a ClientConn's name resolution as one coherent session across controlled network transitions. Preserve resolver continuation state, provide a stable quiescence boundary, and atomically publish retained state on resume without disrupting established RPC behavior.

DNS, manual, and delegating resolvers must suspend according to their continuation models. Resolvers without native support return a deterministic unsupported outcome without changing callback or closure behavior. Treat delegating target and proxy children atomically, rolling back or terminating if either cannot suspend.

Return a receipt only after every preceding or racing callback is classified as published or retained. It is single-use and bound to one ClientConn and session; reject foreign, stale, or consumed receipts deterministically. Resume coalesces retained updates into one newer generation and atomically exposes complete resolver, balancer, connectivity, and picker state. Report later retained errors without changing that generation.

Idle entry, closure, cancellation, and resolver replacement terminate sessions without reviving discarded resolution or transport state. Unary and streaming attempts observe one complete picker generation per attempt, preserve established attempts and stream identity without duplicate transports, and cannot advance resolution while suspended.
